title: Sign symmetry of a truncated sum
statement: For every $n\ge 0$ and every sign vector $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, let $S_n(x)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$, with the coefficient interpreted as the real reciprocal of $\sqrt n$. Truncating a real number to the interval $[-1,1]$ is odd, so truncating this normalized sum after negating every coordinate gives the negative of its truncated value at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a sign vector of length $n$
